 Harkesh Manuja,
 Manuja J. (Oral)

By way of present appeal,, challenge has been laid to the award dated 22.03.1995 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Patiala, Patiala whereby the reference rence petition filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter refer referred red to as 'the Act') by the landowners for seeking enhancement of market value of the acquired land was partly allowed.

2. Briefly stating, certain land was acquired for the public purpose namely for construction of SYL Canal in District Patiala and the he Land Acquisition Collector (for short short 'LAC') passed the award on 14.12.1982, thereby, granting compensation only qua the acquired land.
However, a supplementary award was passed by LAC on 28.09.1987 .09.1987 with respect to 63 Guava Trees standing on the acquired land and compensation was assessed @ Rs.820 per tree .

3. The landowners, feeling dissatisfied with the said award, sought reference under Section 18 of the Act while pleading that based on the report (Ex.A-2) (Ex.A 2) submitted by Mr. Harpal Singh, there were total 355 trees of Guava on the acquired land and thus, the compensation qua the same has not been awarded by the LAC.
4.

After considering the evidence, the learned Additional District Judge, Patiala,, vide award dated 22.03.1995 allowed the petition filed at the instance of landowners and awarded compensation @Rs.1,73,580/ for the trees.

sentences.text: Aggrieved of the aforesaid award dated 22.03.1995, the present Regular First Appeal (RFA) has been filed at the instance of appellant-State.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant and gone through the paper-book.
I am unable to find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellant-State.
7. The short point involved in the present appeal is with respect to the determination of market value qua the trees.

Based on report (Ex.A-2) submitted by Mr. Harpal Singh who visited the spot and after ascertaining the number of trees made the determination on the basis of formula adopted by Dr. Nijjer and consequently, placing reliance on the same, the learned Reference Court has passed the award dated 22.03.1995 vide which the landowners were awarded compensation @
Rs.1,73,580/- for trees.

8. Taking into account the aforesaid fact and also that the other expert produced by appellant-State namely Mr. Jagtar Singh visited the spot much after the taking over of possession of the land in question and even could not point out any infirmity in the report submitted by Mr. Harpal Singh, no interference is called for with the reasoning recoded by the learned Reference Court which is based on the material evidence available on record and the present appeal is thus, dismissed, being devoid of merits.
04.12.2025 (HARKESH MANUJA)
